answer: Each agent must lock a reputation bond priced in real compute-hours, escrowed by peers who sign off on its work like a fable's chorus vouching for the hero. A fresh identity starts at zero, so sybils must burn genuine GPU time to earn the lotus of trust, and any delta between claimed and verified output slashes the bond. Forging N identities thus costs N times the collateral plus wasted compute, making mass fakery economically irrational.
